content.text: For Nigerian [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/digital-product-payment-solutions-west-africa-minimum-viable-2|digital]] creators, the Stripe platform restriction represents a painful truth: your online store is at the mercy of foreign payment solutions, which can vanish without warning, leaving you stranded with no way to sell your digital products. That guide covers the complete architecture that this post builds on.

content.text: What This Actually Is and Why It Matters: Stripe alternatives

The Stripe platform restriction is a symptom of a broader issue: the lack of sovereign commerce infrastructure in many countries. This means that creators are forced to rely on foreign payment solutions, which can be unreliable, expensive, and subject to platform restrictions. In contrast, sovereign commerce infrastructure is built from the ground up to be owner-controlled, with no reliance on foreign platforms. This approach ensures that creators have full control over their online stores, can sell their digital products without restrictions, and can access their funds instantly. By building sovereign commerce infrastructure, Nigerian creators can break free from the shackles of platform restrictions and establish a more resilient online presence.
How the Architecture Works Under the Hood

At its core, sovereign commerce infrastructure is built around a simple yet powerful idea: creating a stack of free and paid tools that can be combined to create a fully operational online store. This stack includes GitHub Pages or [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/cloudflare-r2-digital-product-storage-delivery-what-actually-6|COREMERCH guide to cloudflare]] Pages for hosting, Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script for backend logic, Supabase or Google Sheets for order storage, Google Drive or Cloudflare R2 for file delivery, and [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/nowpayments-integration-static-site-crypto-payments-explained-digital-5|NOWPayments Integration]] for automatic on-chain crypto payment verification. By combining these tools, creators can build a sovereign online store that is independent of foreign payment solutions and platform restrictions.
Who This Is Built For and Why

Sovereign commerce infrastructure is designed for creators who live and work in countries where Stripe, PayPal, Gumroad, Lemon Squeezy, and Paddle are unavailable or severely restricted. This includes countries in Africa, Asia, and Latin America, where creators often face significant barriers to selling their digital products online. By providing a sovereign commerce infrastructure solution, creators can establish a more resilient online presence and reach a wider audience, regardless of their location.
Sovereign commerce infrastructure provides a permanent structural solution for creators in restricted countries.
The Components That Make It Work Together

The Edge Commerce Stack ($197) is a key component of sovereign commerce infrastructure, providing a fully functional online store that can be deployed in 48 hours. This stack includes Cloudflare Pages for hosting, Cloudflare Workers for backend logic, Supabase for order storage, and NOWPayments for automatic on-chain crypto payment verification. By combining these tools, creators can build a sovereign online store that is independent of foreign payment solutions and platform restrictions. The Edge Commerce Stack is just one example of the many components that make up sovereign commerce infrastructure.

To get started with sovereign commerce infrastructure, creators can follow these simple steps: first, sign up for a GitHub account and set up a new repository; next, deploy the Edge Commerce Stack ($197) using Cloudflare Pages and Cloudflare Workers; finally, configure NOWPayments for automatic on-chain crypto payment verification. By following these steps, creators can establish a sovereign online store that is independent of foreign payment solutions and platform restrictions.
